name: Orbit Products Reader
description: Reads the four ephemeris CONTAINERS this stack round-trips — SPK (NAIF DAF, segment types 8, 9 and 13), SP3-c/d, Code-500 and scenario-epoch STK ephemeris — plus CCSDS-OEM keyword-value notation, and projects them onto SDS $OEM with the container's own facts carried out separately as $NCD. A container is a wire format, not a standard: the state history becomes $OEM and the file-level header, comment area, segment address ranges and accuracy block become the native-container descriptor, so a read-then-write cycle reproduces the source instead of inventing header values. Each container is evaluated by the interpolation rule it declares, never by a rule this module picked, and no time-scale conversion happens here: epochs stay on the scale the container named and that name is carried out with them. A malformed container is a named status, never a trap and never a NaN. Converts public-format Vimpel osculating element tables to analytic J2000 epoch OPM states with source provenance; no differenced velocity or covariance is invented. Converts SP Vector/Covariance Messages, legacy V2.0 text or superseded $VCM records, to $OCM without deriving uncertainty or splitting the ballistic coefficient. Reads ESA Sentinel-1/2/3 Earth Explorer orbit files (EOF) to an Earth-fixed $OEM, and reads and writes NAIF CK type 3 kernels as $AEM against a supplied spacecraft clock kernel; every request option travels in an $NCD or in the record itself.
tagline: SPK, SP3, Code-500, STK and CCSDS-OEM containers in; $OEM states and an $NCD descriptor out.

sequentialJustification.detail: Reading a container is one forward pass over one resident buffer into one state series, and the projection onto $OEM and $NCD is a second pass over that series. The module spawns nothing, opens nothing, shares nothing between invocations and holds no state after one: everything it can answer is already in the frame it was handed, so there is no work to fan out and never will be.

inputPorts.description: The container to read, as a size-prefixed SDS $NCD descriptor followed IMMEDIATELY by the container's exact bytes in the same frame. $NCD carries the file's facts and its SOURCE_SHA256, not its payload, so the payload rides with the descriptor that describes it: the size prefix gives the descriptor's exact length and therefore the offset the container starts at, and SOURCE_SHA256 and SOURCE_BYTE_LENGTH are checked against those trailing bytes when the caller declared them, which is what makes the pairing provable rather than assumed. FORMAT selects the reader; UNSPECIFIED asks this module to identify the container from its own leading bytes and report what it found.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described container's bytes appended to the frame.

outputPorts.description: SDS $OEM envelope carrying every state history the container described, one data block per object: an SPK segment per body, an SP3 satellite per block, an OEM block per block. Positions are kilometres and velocities kilometres per second, as the IDL fixes. SP3's per-state clock bias and rate ride on EPHEMERIS_DATA_LINES and the NAIF integer target and centre codes on the block, so nothing the container stated about identity or clocks is dropped on the way into the record.

SDS $NCD envelope carrying the half of the container that $OEM cannot hold: the resolved FORMAT, the internal file name, the comment area, the segment descriptors with their address ranges, the SP3 header accuracy block, the scenario-epoch parameters or the Code-500 header, and the SHA-256 of the bytes this run actually read. A writer that is handed the $OEM and this descriptor can reproduce the source container; a writer handed only the $OEM has to invent its header.

inputPorts.description: The same frame read_container takes: a size-prefixed SDS $NCD descriptor followed immediately by the container's exact bytes. A caller that only wants to know what a file IS sends the descriptor with FORMAT unset and gets back what this module identified.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described container's bytes appended to the frame.

outputPorts.description: SDS $NCD envelope with everything this module resolved from the container filled in, including the format it identified when the caller did not name one. This is the surface that answers "what is this file" without materialising its states, and the honest place to see a disagreement: a descriptor that came in claiming one format and goes out resolved as another says so here.

inputPorts.description: An Intelsat eleven-parameter (IESS-412) ephemeris file as SES and Intelsat publish it, as a size-prefixed SDS $NCD descriptor with FORMAT PROVIDER_DEFINED and PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME "ses-i11", SOURCE_SHA256 and SOURCE_BYTE_LENGTH declared, followed immediately by the file's exact bytes in the same frame.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described container's bytes appended to the frame.

outputPorts.description: SDS $OEM envelope with one Earth-fixed (FIXED_EARTH) block on UTC: the eleven-parameter model evaluated from the element epoch to the file's stated end of validity (170 hours when it states none) every 300 s, positions in kilometres and velocities in kilometres per second (analytic derivatives). OBJECT_NAME is the satellite name the file states; no catalog number is supplied. The block COMMENT records the elements and how closely the file's own printed prediction is reproduced; a file whose printed prediction is not reproduced to its printed precision is refused.
The input $NCD descriptor, unchanged: its SOURCE_CID and SOURCE_SHA256 lead back to the file.

methods.displayName: Convert an SP Vector/Covariance Message to OCM

inputPorts.description: The legacy SP Vector/Covariance Message V2.0 text, as a size-prefixed SDS $NCD descriptor (FORMAT PROVIDER_DEFINED, PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME "vcm-v2-text", SOURCE_SHA256 and SOURCE_BYTE_LENGTH declared) followed immediately by the exact message bytes in the same frame. Lines not beginning with "<>" are communication-system insertions and are skipped.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described container's bytes appended to the frame.

outputPorts.description: SDS $OCM: the J2K state as the trajectory in EME2000 about EARTH, with CCSDS 502.0-B-3 keywords where the VCM field means the same thing (gravity model and truncation, lunar/solar bodies, fixed F10.7, mean F10.7 and ap, SEDR, weighted RMS, revolution number, TAI-UTC, UT1-UTC). Fields without a CCSDS equivalent travel verbatim in USER_DEFINED_PARAMETERS with their units in the name: the ballistic coefficient (the product Cd*A/m, not split), the SRP coefficient, U,V,W sigmas, the equinoctial-element covariance (not converted to a Cartesian covariance), and the ECI and EFG copies of the state.
The exact input $NCD descriptor, which keeps the source hash so every field of the original message stays recoverable.

inputPorts.description: One superseded SDS $VCM record. REF_FRAME, CENTER_NAME, TIME_SYSTEM and STATE_VECTOR with EPOCH are required; they are copied, never assumed.

outputPorts.description: SDS $OCM: the record's state in its own REF_FRAME and CENTER_NAME, CCSDS physical properties (mass, drag and SRP areas and coefficients), GM and revolution number; SGP4 terms, sigmas, covariance and element sets travel verbatim in USER_DEFINED_PARAMETERS.

inputPorts.description: An ESA Earth Explorer orbit file (Sentinel-1/2/3 AUX_POEORB, AUX_RESORB, AUX_PREORB) as a size-prefixed SDS $NCD with FORMAT PROVIDER_DEFINED and PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME "sentinel-eof", followed immediately by the file's exact bytes in the same frame. The $NCD is also the request: START_TIME and STOP_TIME, when set, select the inclusive window of states read, stated on the file's own Time_Reference. SOURCE_SHA256 and SOURCE_BYTE_LENGTH are checked against the bytes when declared.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described file's bytes appended to the frame.

outputPorts.description: SDS $OEM with one block in the file's own Earth-fixed frame (FIXED_EARTH, the file names no realization), kilometres and kilometres per second, one state per OSV with the epoch text the file wrote on its Time_Reference (no time-scale conversion). OBJECT_NAME is the mission the file names; no catalog number is supplied. The block COMMENT declares what $OEM has no column for: the per-OSV TAI and UT1 stamps, the orbit number and the Quality flag counts.

SDS $NCD recording the source: the internal file name, the producing system and creator, the creation date, the frame and time reference the file named, the file type and validity as the one segment, the coverage read and the SHA-256 of the bytes.

inputPorts.description: A NAIF CK (DAF/CK) as a size-prefixed SDS $NCD with FORMAT PROVIDER_DEFINED and PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME "naif-ck", followed immediately by the kernel's exact bytes. The $NCD is also the request: START_TIME and STOP_TIME select the inclusive window of records on the clock's time system, and SEGMENTS entries select the segments whose NAME and/or TARGET_NAIF_ID (the instrument) match; no entries selects every segment. A selected segment that is not CK type 3 is refused by name.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described file's bytes appended to the frame.

inputPorts.description: The spacecraft clock kernel (type 1 SCLK text kernel) as a size-prefixed SDS $NCD with FORMAT PROVIDER_DEFINED and PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME "naif-sclk", followed immediately by the kernel's exact bytes. SEGMENTS[0].TARGET_NAIF_ID, when set, is the spacecraft clock id (-76); without it the clock is NAIF's rule, the instrument id divided by 1000.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described file's bytes appended to the frame.

outputPorts.description: SDS $AEM with one segment per CK interpolation interval: ATTITUDE_DIR A2B, REF_FRAME_A the segment's reference frame (a NAIF built-in name or the decimal frame code), REF_FRAME_B the instrument code, ATTITUDE_TYPE QUATERNION or QUATERNION/ANGVEL, one explicit epoch per record on the clock's time system (TDB or TT, no conversion), the quaternion as CCSDS (Q1 Q2 Q3 QC) from A to B (the NAIF vector part negated) and the angular velocity in deg/s expressed in REF_FRAME_A.
SDS $NCD recording the file: the internal file name, the comment area, every segment with its instrument, frame, type, addresses and span, the coverage read and the SHA-256 of the bytes.

inputPorts.description: SDS $AEM to write as a CK, one CK segment per AEM segment. REF_FRAME_A is the reference frame (a NAIF built-in inertial name or a decimal frame code), REF_FRAME_B the instrument (a nonzero decimal code), OBJECT_NAME the segment identifier (at most 40 printable characters), ATTITUDE_DIR A2B, ATTITUDE_TYPE QUATERNION or QUATERNION/ANGVEL with ANGVEL_FRAME REF_FRAME_A, TIME_SYSTEM the clock's, one explicit epoch per line. A compact-form segment, a B2A direction, another attitude type, a non-unit quaternion and a TIME_SYSTEM that is not the clock's are each refused by name.
The spacecraft clock kernel, framed as for normalize_naif_ck. Its time system (TDB or TT) is the one the $AEM epochs must be stated on.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described file's bytes appended to the frame.

inputPorts.description: Optional $NCD: INTERNAL_FILE_NAME (at most 60 printable characters) and COMMENT_AREA become the kernel's internal name and comment area. FORMAT, when set, must be PROVIDER_DEFINED "naif-ck".

outputPorts.description: The kernel in the frame normalize_naif_ck reads: a size-prefixed SDS $NCD (the written segments, addresses and the SHA-256 of the kernel) followed immediately by the kernel's exact bytes, DAF/CK, LTL-IEEE, type 3, one interval per segment.

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $NCD envelope, with the described file's bytes appended to the frame.
